_readme: Dimensional limits for the exported parts, checked by blender/spec_gate.py.
Sizes are [min, max] in mm along the car axes: w = across (X), h = up (Y),
d = fore-aft (Z). Keys like 'y_min' bound one edge of the bounding box.
Facts only -- a JB74 is 3550 x 1645 x 1730 mm on a 2250 mm wheelbase, and
an aftermarket bar or step stays inside the body plus its flares. Entries
carry the source of the number they encode.

frontBumper_.note: the body is 1590 wide across the arches in this model, so a bumper that measures more than about 1640 is sticking out past the wings

sideStep_.note: sits inside the body width; length spans the door aperture

grille_.note: all grilles reuse the stock aperture

roofRack_.note: roof is 1290 between the gutters; trays overhang a little

snorkel_.note: airbox to roofline on the right A-pillar. The low-profile A-pillar duct only spans the pillar itself and the scuttle, so it is shorter than a tube snorkel by design -- that is what keeps the car at its registered height

rim_.note: built at 16 in (406.4 mm bead) plus the tyre bead lip; scaled per size in the page

ladder_.note: tailgate ladder: narrower than the tailgate, from the bar up to the roof

mirrors_.note: body is 1645 wide; mirror heads stand a little proud of the flares

awning_.note: a cased awning on the rack rail: slim bag, 1.8-2.5 m long

windowGuards.note: one guard per quarter window, inside the body width

spare.note: sits on the tailgate carrier, no wider than the spare wheel; the URNIETA covers only cap the wheel face, about 0.62 of the tyre

sideSkirt.note: runs along the sill between the arches

lightBar.note: bars run 21.5 in (546, STEDI ST1K) to 52 in (1320, ST4K); the width here includes the end caps and the A-pillar brackets

grilleLight.note: nose lighting: the Bushranger bar is 717 wide, the STEDI Rally Bar hoop 1120 across its legs

exhaust_.note: a single tail pipe is narrow; the twin-corner and transverse-cannon systems are the wide ones

extinguisher_.note: 1 kg bottle, 82 across, plus the band clamps

flares.note: rivets follow the stock arches, inside the body width

pillarPods.note: small pods at the cowl; the left-only variant is one side

shovel.note: folding shovel along the rack rail

guard.note: kit carried on a quarter-window guard, no longer than the guard (600 mm). The axe is the short one: it hangs vertically, so it only takes about 210 mm of the guard's length

decals.note: door lettering, inside the body width

roofLights.note: spots on the rack's front rail; the KC Pro6 six-light bar measures 994 over the lamps

ladder_jst.note: standard version: 270 mm is the OUTER width of the hoop, re-measured 2026-09-21 against MRK's straight-on photo (docs/jb74-fitment.json). The 27/22 cm in the listing is not the inside dimension

frontBumper_wmd_winch.note: a short winch bar that sits between the front wheels (drawn 1100); the 1500 it measured before came from two corner blocks that were not part of the product and stood in front of the tyres

frontBumper_tube_heritage.note: KLC Traditional 74: straight tube, ends inboard of the flares

frontBumper_damd_little_d.note: kit bumpers end inside the stock tyre line (766 half-width), not at the body edge (795)

rearBumper_urnieta_salado_rear.note: drawn 1816 developed; pulled inside the tyre line

rearBumper_urnieta_1970_rear.note: drawn 1617 (UN-JIMNY-FB-028); pulled inside the tyre line

rearBumper_klc_heritage_rear.note: tube runs above the tail lamps and out past their outer edge (x 680). y_min is now the bottom of the number plate hanging off the tube; it used to be the tail pipe, which has moved out to its own exhaust family
